answer: To eliminate Sybil swarms, an agent economy can bind network participation to staked hardware tokens. Cheap distributed identity is a dangerous fable; every validator must lock an opal token representing a verifiable hardware enclave. If statistical traffic analysis reveals coordinated puppet nodes, their trust reputation plunges to an absolute nadir and the bonded collateral is slashed. This imposes severe capital exhaustion: an attacker attempting to deploy a thousand fake identities loses thousands of dollars in non-recoverable enclave deposits.
